name: Patagonia Stories
source: Renowned UX, captured 25/11/2026 (390 and 1280 px, scroll frames for motion)
idea: A magazine-style story index that puts the brand's activism and expedition narratives ahead of its product catalogue, reached from the main shop nav.
archetype: Editorial journal inside a shop
hero: Full-bleed video still of a person in a knit beanie over a winter forest, with the 'patagonia Stories' wordmark in white across the middle (1280). On 390 the hero rendered as a flat grey block at capture time (video not loaded).
layout: Full-bleed hero, then a 'Some Favorites' horizontal rail of story cards (name plus read-time pill, photo on the right, carousel arrow), then full-bleed photo bands between rail rows. A sticky 'Patagonia Stories' header appears on scroll.
type: Sans-serif throughout (logotype and nav); card titles in a light serif-like face, as seen in the 1280 rail.
colour: #000000 (top utility bar), #FFFFFF (header and page), #F4F4F4 (story card background), with the photography supplying almost all colour; hex values are eyeballed from the screenshot, not sampled. The page is black and white, so the photos carry the colour.
imagery: Real expedition and outdoor photography of named athletes and climbers, plus night-sky and landscape frames.
media: Hero video (autoplay expected, playback not observed at capture); still images on cards and bands.
motion: Hero video; horizontal rail with a carousel arrow; sticky header that reveals on scroll (observed in the scroll capture). Easing not observed.

sections.description: Full-bleed video with the 'patagonia Stories' wordmark, under a utility bar that links 'Activism' and 'Stories'.
'Some Favorites' horizontal rail; each card gives the person or story name and a read-time pill.
Full-bleed dark night-sky photograph as a pause between card rows.
The shop nav (Gift Guide, Women's, Men's, Packs & Gear, Used Clothing) sits above the stories, so the story index is one click from products.

steal: Put the brand's own story index in the main shop nav, labelled by its content ('Stories'), not in the footer.
Give each story card a read-time pill so a visitor knows the commitment before opening it.
Open the index with a full-bleed film or photo, then drop into a rail of cards with names as the headline.
Keep a sticky header that reappears when the visitor scrolls back up through a long editorial page.

name: Our Place About (A Note from Shiza)

layout: Hero, then a two-column split: left column 'A Note from Shiza' (body copy and signature), right column a full-height photo of a woman cooking with a red patterned sleeve. Below, a centred line 'For connections made across the kitchen table.' followed by the product row.
type: Serif display for headings ('Welcome to Our Place', 'A Note from Shiza', 'For connections made across the kitchen table.'), sans-serif body.
colour: #FBF9F5 (cream page), #3A3430 (charcoal text), with saturated colour from the photography (red patterned fabric, green cookware); hex values are eyeballed, not sampled.
imagery: Real people cooking and eating, the founder photographed at work, product shots on cream backgrounds.
media: Still photography; no video observed on the about page.
motion: not observed

sections.description: Full-bleed table photo with serif headline and eyebrow line.
'A Note from Shiza': first-person paragraphs, then the signature line 'Shiza Shahid, Co-Founder' (preceded by a dash).
'For connections made across the kitchen table.' sets the brand's purpose in one serif statement.
Cookware grid on cream, the catalogue the note leads into.

steal: Sign the origin note with the founder's full name and role under the last line, in the same column as the text.
Set a cooking photo of the founder beside the note, not a stock image.
Follow the note with one short serif promise line, then the product row.

name: Brightland About Us
source: Renowned UX, captured 25/11/2026 (390 and 1280 px, scroll frames for motion)
idea: An origin page that states sourcing in short declarative headlines, each set beside its own photograph in alternating halves, linked from the main nav beside the store locator.
archetype: Honest provenance page
hero: Full-bleed sunlit still life of olive oil, vinegar and honey bottles with oranges and a grapefruit half, headline 'You bring the food. We'll bring the sunshine.' in a condensed serif (1280). The capture shows the same hero as the brand's homepage; the about-page body starts below it.
layout: Hero, centred intro 'Welcome to the Golden State' paragraph, then alternating 50/50 blocks: product photo left and headline right ('Fueled by sunshine, great soil and the highest standards.'), then text left and olive-branch photo right ('Consciously crafted from the best stuff in nature.').
type: Condensed serif headlines, sans-serif body in a light weight.
colour: #FDF6F2 (cream intro band), #FFFFFF (text blocks), #E2481E (red-orange promo bar, approx), #000000 text; hex values eyeballed, not sampled. The warm bands and orange product photography carry the palette.
imagery: Product still lifes with citrus and herbs, close-up olive branches, bottles with label detail visible.
media: Still photography; product bottle video loop on the homepage was not checked here.
motion: not observed

sections.description: Sunlit still life with the one-line promise.
'Welcome to the Golden State' paragraph: origin in two sentences.
'Fueled by sunshine, great soil and the highest standards.' beside a product photo.
'Consciously crafted from the best stuff in nature.' beside an olive-tree photo, naming family farmers and beekeepers.

steal: Write each origin claim as one short declarative headline and set it over or beside its own photo.
Alternate image and text halves down the page so each claim gets its own visual rhythm.
Link 'Our Story' in the main nav next to 'Find in Store', so origin sits at shopping level.

name: Apple Environment
source: Renowned UX, captured 25/11/2026 (390 and 1280 px, scroll frames for motion)
idea: A scroll-driven sustainability report where one headline claim, backed by a concrete target against a base year, sits over full-bleed landscape before any product appears.
archetype: Long-form sustainability report
hero: Pale blue-to-white gradient with the '2030' Apple lockup and 'Our planet deserves our best thinking.' over a forest horizon (1280). A pause control sits top right, and a sticky subnav shows 'Environment' and a green '2026 Report (PDF)' pill.
layout: Hero, then full-bleed aerial forest photo with the headline 'Innovation is up. Emissions are down.' and a paragraph on the 75% reduction target against 2015, then a light grey section 'A comprehensive approach. From design to disassembly.'
type: Bold sans-serif display headings (SF-style), regular sans body.
colour: #F5F5F7 (light grey section), #1D1D1F (text), pale blue gradient in the hero; hex values eyeballed, not sampled. Colour comes mostly from the landscape photography.
imagery: Aerial and landscape photography of forests and fog, with a credit line for the project location (Apple's Restore Fund, California).
media: Looping hero (the pause control implies motion; playback itself not observed).
motion: Hero loop with a pause control; full-bleed photo band reads as a scroll pause. Scroll-linked animation not observed.

sections.description: '2030' lockup and the one-line goal on a calm gradient.
Full-bleed landscape with 'Innovation is up. Emissions are down.' and the 75% target against 2015 in the body.
'A comprehensive approach. From design to disassembly.' on light grey, the section that explains how.
Sticky subnav keeps the '2026 Report (PDF)' pill visible for anyone who wants the source.

steal: Lead the story with one measurable target stated against a base year in the body copy.
Give a full-bleed motion hero a visible pause control, so the visitor can stop it.
Keep one 'Report (PDF)' pill in the sticky subnav for the readers who want the source.

name: Christy Dawn Honoring Mother Earth
source: Renowned UX, captured 25/11/2026 (390 and 1280 px, scroll frames for motion)
idea: A values page that opens on one centred serif commitment paragraph, then runs each principle as a photo of real practice (soil, a washing line, a stream), so the page reads as a manifesto, not a checklist.
archetype: Values manifesto
hero: Centred all-caps serif headline 'HONORING MOTHER EARTH' with a four-line intro paragraph on white, then a full-width photo of two pairs of hands holding garden soil (1280).
layout: Centred heading and paragraph; full-width photo; a centred uppercase serif statement under the heading 'Beyond Sustainability'; a split photo row (clothes drying on a line left, a sunlit stream right).
type: All-caps serif for the headline and statement; sans-serif for the 'Beyond Sustainability' heading (observed in the scroll capture); serif body.
colour: #FFFFFF (page), #4E5E4A (sage-green announcement bar, approx), #2B2B2B (text, approx); hex values eyeballed, not sampled. Earthy photography (soil, ivy, sunlit stone) supplies the rest.
imagery: Unposed photos of hands in soil, clothes drying outdoors, rock and water; no studio product shots on the page.
media: Still photographs.
motion: not observed

sections.description: Serif headline and a four-line commitment paragraph.
Hands holding soil as the emotional anchor under the commitment.
'Beyond Sustainability': the brand says sustainability is not enough and names regenerative practice as the next goal.
Split row of real practice (washing line, sunlit stream) that stand in for proof.

steal: Open the values page with one commitment sentence in serif, not a bullet list.
Pair each principle with a photo of real practice (soil, washing line), not a studio shot.
Name the next goal in a bold sentence ('regenerative, not just sustainable') so the page admits its limits.

name: Christy Dawn Journal

type: Serif display for 'Journal' and tile titles; italic serif for filter chips.
colour: #FFFFFF (page), #4E5E4A (sage-green announcement bar, approx), #000000 (text); hex values eyeballed, not sampled. Film-still photography supplies most of the colour.
imagery: Film stills of people in wardrobes, cafés and travel locations, with the series title overlaid in white serif.
media: Video thumbnails (the series are film pieces); playback not observed.
motion: not observed

sections.description: 'Journal' heading over the topic filter row.
Italic topic chips with 'All' at the end, active chip underlined.
Two-column large tiles, each with an overlaid title and a printed title beneath.
Recurring 'Welcome to My Closet' tiles, one per guest, so a new feature joins a known set.

steal: Name recurring features with a fixed format ('Welcome to My Closet with X') so each new one joins a recognisable series.
Filter the archive with italic topic chips ending in 'All', and underline the active one.
Print the feature title under each large tile in the same type for every tile, so the grid reads as one set.

Drop-cap paragraph: what the company does, in plain words, with the acquisition stated in the last sentence.
Three paragraphs naming both founders, the 2001 start, and the 2021 acquisition as a factual step.
Short 'Culture' section ending in a hiring link.

State an acquisition or ownership change as one factual sentence in the story, not in a legal footer.
Open the about page with a drop-cap intro paragraph so the reader enters the text.

name: Apple Store, Buy iPhone

Five text tabs that narrow the model set (All Models, iPhone Picks, Ways to Save, Only at Apple, Setup and Support).
Horizontal card carousel: render, colour dots, monthly price, lease line, Buy button on each card.

name: Stripe home

imagery: Real-looking application UI screenshots and 3D wireframe icon objects in the feature grid.
media: Static UI panels and short-looped animated panels; logo strip at the top of the feature band.
motion: From the 1280 sheet (83 frames, the longest run): the headline stays put at the top while the app panel moves up and the logo band (OpenAI, Vercel, Figma and others) slides in above. 'A new species of product tool.' then appears with a row of wireframe 3D objects that fade in one by one. 'Intake and integrations' keeps its headline on the left while product cards (triage, Slack-style threads) slide in on the right. 'Planning and monitoring' animates a chart panel into place. 'AI and automations' ends with an agent UI. Timing is rough, read from frame order.

sections.description: Headline, subline and an app window that sits partly below the fold.
Customer logos slide in above the feature stack as social proof.
One-line positioning with a grid of wireframe objects that fade in per feature.
A feature headline stays on the left while its product cards slide in on the right.
Agent UI and automation panel closes the scroll.

steal: Pin each feature's headline on one side and slide its product panel in on the other, so the visitor reads and sees the product in one view.
Show the product working (cards arriving, a chart drawing in) rather than a still screenshot, so the scroll is the demo.
Put customer logos in a band above the feature stack, so social proof is seen before the first claim.

name: Stripe Sessions conference page
source: Renowned UX, captured 25/11/2026 (390 and 1280 px, scroll frames for motion)
idea: A generative ribbon artwork carries the whole page, and the sections between it swap their media as the reader moves through a sticky list, so an event page reads like a film with chapters.
archetype: generative-art event page with sticky chapter list
hero: Off-white page, the headline 'The internet economy conference' in deep purple at left, date 'May 4-6, 2027' and venue 'Moscone North & South, San Francisco' at right, and a large rounded panel of a 3D ribbon gradient (purple, blue, pink, orange) filling the width below (measured from the 1280 still).
layout: Full-width hero with generative art panel; then a two-column sticky section (left list, right media); horizontal carousels for speakers and passes; a sponsor grid at the foot.
type: Large sans display headline, tight tracking, deep purple on off-white (from memory: a custom Stripe sans).
colour: Estimated by eye from the still, not sampled: #F8F6F8 (page), #1A0536 (headline and buttons), #7A3CFF to #FF4FD8 to #FFB020 (ribbon gradient). One brand purple plus the ribbon gradient.
imagery: Procedural 3D ribbon artwork (no photography in the hero), then event video and photos of the venue in the chapter panels.
media: Generative art that re-forms with scroll, a looping event video, and still photography of the venue and speakers.
motion: From the 1280 sheet (69 frames): the ribbon artwork re-forms across the first several scroll steps while the headline holds. 'Why attend' then pins on the left with a video panel on the right; as each left-column item becomes active ('Join main stage keynotes', 'Build an agenda around your business priorities', 'Expand your skills', 'Test ideas, ask questions') the right panel swaps to that item's still or video. The 'Speakers' carousel slides horizontally, enlarging the centre card (a speaker named Ben Gilbert). 'Conference passes' and 'Agenda at a glance' use the same ribbon art as a sticky decoration. Timing is rough, read from frame order.

sections.description: Headline and date block over a full-width ribbon artwork that re-forms with scroll.
Left column of short chapters that each light up as the reader scrolls; right column swaps the matching media.
Portrait cards slide sideways and the centre card enlarges.
Three or four pass cards with price and a single action, using the ribbon art as a backdrop.
Day-by-day list beside a sticky ribbon, then a sponsor grid.

steal: Let the hero artwork change shape with scroll rather than standing still, so the first screen already rewards scrolling.
Pair a sticky chapter list with a media panel that swaps per item, so each reason to attend gets its own picture without new pages.
Show speakers as a sideways carousel where the active card enlarges, so the browsing action carries the narrative.

name: Vercel home page
source: Renowned UX, captured 25/11/2026 (390 and 1280 px, scroll frames for motion)
idea: A quiet hero with one mark gives way to customer-proof cards that slide in one at a time, each headline naming a customer type, so the scroll moves from brand to use case to proof.
archetype: minimal hero with customer-case scroll
hero: Off-white page, 'Agentic Infrastructure' headline left, a single large black triangle mark in the centre on a soft shadow, three short lines at right ('For coding agents', 'To ship apps and agents', 'Automated by agents'), 'Deploy now' and 'Talk to sales' buttons, and a customer logo band (Meta, DoorDash, OpenAI, SpaceX, The Weather Company, Polymarket) along the bottom (measured from the 1280 still).
layout: Three-column hero with the mark in the middle; logo band; then full-width headline sections each with a product card on one side.
type: Large grotesque sans with tight tracking, sentence case (from memory: Geist).
colour: Estimated by eye from the still, not sampled: #FAFAFA (page), #000000 (mark and Deploy now), #171717 (headline), #E5E5E5 (shadow). Achromatic; colour comes only from customer logos and the product cards.
imagery: One abstract black mark; then product UI cards (chat, a Notion-style panel, a docs site, a Zapier-style sign-in) and small illustrated cards.
media: Static product card images and a few looped UI animations; no video observed.
motion: From the 1280 sheet (54 frames): the triangle mark holds centre for the first several steps while the logo band slides up and out. The headline then changes to 'Build agents on infrastructure that thinks like them' with a Notion-style product card sliding in on the left. 'Ship apps that scale from zero to millions instantly' takes over with a Zapier-style card. 'Host platforms that serve every customer' follows with a documentation card. 'Recently shipped' tiles (Agents, Backends, Sandbox) rise in a grid. The page ends on 'Built by you, or your agents' with a Deploy button and the footer. Timing is rough, read from frame order.

sections.description: Headline, one mark, three benefit lines and two CTAs.
Customer logos as social proof directly under the hero.
A headline naming a customer type with that customer's product card, one per scroll stage.
Grid of short case tiles (Agents, Backends, Sandbox) that rise in.
One line with a Deploy button and a secondary action, then footer.

steal: Use one sparse brand mark in the hero and let the scroll bring in customer product cards, so the proof replaces decoration as the reader goes down.
Give each scroll stage a headline that names the buyer type (for example 'Host platforms that serve every customer') with a card that shows that buyer's product.
Close with a one-line call to action and one primary button rather than a second feature section.
